extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (appellants, patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing ex parte appeals to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (PTAB), including reply briefs, supplemental examiner's answers, oral hearing requests, remands, and Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examiner's answer responding to a reply brief (37 CFR 41.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a new issue raised in a reply brief must be approved by the Technology Center (TC) Director or designee. 37 CFR 41.43(a)(2) prohibits a supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a reply brief from including a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a reply brief is filed, a supplemental answer may respond to new issues but cannot present new grounds of rejection; any new ground responding to a reply brief must be by reopening prosecution (see MPEP § 1207.04). A supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a reply brief requires TC Director/designee approval. Appellant may file another reply within two months of mailing of the supplemental examiner’s answer (two-month period not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a), but may be extendable under 1.136(b) for patent applications or 1.550(c) for reexamination proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner option to withdraw final rejection and reopen prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to a reply brief, the examiner may withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution to respond to the reply brief (see MPEP § 1207.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal of the final rejection and entry of a new ground of rejection requires approval from the supervisory patent examiner, and that approval must be indicated in the Office action setting forth the new ground (See MPEP § 1207.04). Reopening prosecution is an alternative to issuing a supplemental examiner’s answer and is the proper means to present a new ground of rejection after a reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment/entry of a reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The acknowledgment of receipt and entry of a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 is an indication by the examiner that no further response by the examiner is deemed necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An indication that certain rejections have been withdrawn as a result of the reply brief is permitted and is not, by itself, a supplemental examiner’s answer. Such an indication of a change in status of claims does not give appellant the right to file another reply brief. The examiner may make the indication on form PTOL-90.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request requirements (37 CFR 41.47(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant desires an oral hearing, appellant must file, as a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING,' a written request accompanied by the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(3) within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/32 may be used. The two-month period may only be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(b) (patent applications) or 37 CFR 1.550(c) (ex parte reexamination). If the request is not filed in a separate paper with that caption, is untimely, or lacks the fee, the appeal will be assigned for decision on the briefs without an oral hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing scheduling and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral hearing is held, oral argument will ordinarily be limited to twenty minutes for appellant and fifteen minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant argues first and may reserve rebuttal. Appellant may request additional time in advance; the senior member of the panel decides on additional time. Telephone argument may be requested (appellant bears telephone cost). Hearings may be rescheduled on written request but postponements are discouraged and require convincing reasons. Failure to confirm or appear leads to removal from hearing docket and decision on briefs; no refund of hearing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of evidence and arguments at oral hearing (37 CFR 41.47(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: At the oral hearing, appellant may only rely on evidence that has been previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present argument that has been relied upon in the brief or reply brief, except upon a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good cause may permit reliance on a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court. The primary examiner is likewise limited to evidence and argument relied upon in the answer or supplemental answer except as permitted by good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may decide an appeal without oral hearing (37 CFR 41.47(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the submission of a request for oral hearing, if the Board decides that a hearing is not necessary, the Board will so notify appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where hearing may be unnecessary: remand to the examiner is necessary, or it is clear the rejection(s) cannot be sustained. The Board's decision to forego a hearing is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public admittance at oral hearings in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the appeal involves reexamination proceedings, oral hearings are open to the public as observers unless the appellant requests closure and presents valid reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party observers must obtain prior written permission from the Board to observe the hearing. Appellant can request closure and must present valid reasons for such request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner participation in oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the primary examiner wishes to appear and present oral argument before the Board, a request to present oral argument must be set forth in a separate letter on a form PTOL-90 using form paragraph 12.163.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.163 only if an oral hearing has been requested and the primary examiner intends to present oral argument. The examiner will be allowed 15 minutes to reply and may present a statement clearly setting forth the examiner’s position. The primary examiner may only rely on argument and evidence relied upon in the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer except as permitted by good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction transfer to the Board (37 CFR 41.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over the proceeding passes to the Board upon transmittal of the file, including all briefs and examiner’s answers, to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the file is incomplete or noncompliant, the Board may relinquish jurisdiction to permit completion. Prior to entry of a decision, the Director may sua sponte remand the proceeding to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for transfer of jurisdiction to the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The application file and jurisdiction are normally transferred to the Board after either (A) two months from the examiner’s answer (plus mail room time) if no reply brief has been filed, or (B) after the examiner notifies the appellant that the reply brief has been entered and that the application will be forwarded to the Board (e.g., by mailing a PTOL-90 with form paragraph 12.181).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment or other paper relating to the appeal filed after transfer but prior to decision may be considered by the examiner only if the case is remanded for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection (37 CFR 41.50(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may remand a case to the examiner for further consideration of a rejection (e.g., where pertinence of references is not clear) or for other examiner action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental examiner’s answer written in response to such remand may set forth a new ground of rejection (see MPEP § 1207.03). If remand is for further consideration of a rejection, the appellant must, within two months of the supplemental examiner’s answer, either (A) reopen prosecution (file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with/without amendment or affidavits/evidence) or (B) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41; failure to do so may result in sua sponte dismissal of the appeal as to the remanded claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for supplemental examiner’s answers (¶ 12.184 and ¶ 12.185)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶12.184 and ¶12.185 are form paragraphs for preparing a supplemental examiner’s answer after a remand from the Board: 12.184 for 'No option to Reopen Prosecution' and 12.185 for 'On Remand FOR FURTHER CONSIDERATION OF A REJECTION'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both forms require insertion of date and reasons in brackets and require approval/signature of the TC Director or designee. 12.185 explicitly notifies appellant of the TWO MONTH options (reopen prosecution or maintain appeal) and states time-extension limitations under 1.136(a)/(b) and 1.550(c). Examiner notes explain bracket content and approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by Board to consider amendment (1211.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has no obligation to consider new or amended claims submitted while it has jurisdiction, but a proposed amendment filed after the filing of a brief that cancels claims (where cancellation does not affect scope of other claims) or rewrites dependent claims into independent form may be remanded for consideration by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposed amendment effectively abandons the appeal (e.g., cancels appealed claims), the amendment must be entered and the Chief Clerk notified so the case can be removed from the Board’s docket. See MPEP § 1206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to consider affidavits or declarations (1211.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations filed with the filing of a notice of appeal but before jurisdiction passes to the Board will be considered only if the appellant shows under 37 CFR 1.116(e) why they are necessary and were not earlier presented. Affidavits or declarations filed after notice of appeal but before Board decision generally are not for the examiner to consider unless the examiner determines they overcome all rejections under appeal and necessary showings are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such evidence has not been treated by the examiner, the Board may remand to permit the examiner to consider it. The Board does not customarily remand affidavits/declarations submitted with requests for rehearing where no rejection under 41.50(b) has been made; such submissions are treated as arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand for further search (1211.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remand to the examiner for further search should be extremely rare. A remand to the examiner extends pendency and may necessitate patent-term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such a remand is necessary, the Board should conduct a search of at least one subclass and cite art from that subclass to demonstrate the basis for concluding that a search in that area would be material. The art cited need not be art on which a rejection can be based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may order additional briefing (37 CFR 41.50(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may order appellant to additionally brief any matter that the Board considers to be of assistance in reaching a reasoned decision on the pending appeal; appellant will be given a non-extendable time period to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include asking for briefing on applicability of particular case law or of prior art not previously identified. Failure to timely comply may result in sua sponte dismissal of the appeal. The Board’s use of this authority is discretionary and does not preclude remand to the examiner where appropriate; after appellant’s response, a remand may be appropriate to permit examiner response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision may include new grounds of rejection (37 CFR 41.50(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board has knowledge of grounds not involved in the appeal for rejecting any pending claim, it may include a statement of that effect constituting a new ground of rejection; such a new ground is not final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Board makes a new ground of rejection, the appellant, within two months from the date of the decision, must either (1) reopen prosecution by submitting an amendment or new evidence to have the matter reconsidered by the examiner (the new ground is binding on the examiner unless overcome by amendment/new evidence), or (2) request rehearing under § 41.52 addressing the new ground with particularity and stating points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board statement on how a claim may be amended to overcome a rejection (37 CFR 41.50(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The opinion of the Board may include an explicit statement of how a claim on appeal may be amended to overcome a specific rejection; when it does, appellant has the right to amend in conformity and such amendment will overcome that specific rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment in conformity with such statement will overcome the specific rejection but is not itself a guarantee of allowability—an examiner may reject the so-amended claim if the rejection constitutes a new ground (any such new ground must be approved by a TC Director and prominently identified). A remark by the Board that a feature does not appear in a claim is not to be construed as authority to amend unless the Board makes an explicit statement. Appellant’s right to amend under 41.50(c) may be exercised within the period allowed for seeking court review under 37 CFR 1.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to comply with hearing confirmations or Board orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to confirm the hearing within the time required in the notice or waives the hearing, the appeal will be removed from the hearing docket and assigned on brief; no refund of the fee for requesting an oral hearing will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after confirmation, no appearance is made at the scheduled hearing, the appeal will be decided on brief. Appellant should inform the Board early of changes to avoid wasted resources. Failure to timely comply with a Board order to brief matters under 41.50(d) may result in dismissal.
